commits.summary: Countermodels of the pair of versions: five false proofs of agreement, reproduced and handed to the preservation stream
commits.body: The challenge stream's item 1. lib/tests/fixtures/pairing-countermodels holds two versions of five methods that differ when each runs alone on a JVM and that RegressionPair.agree (lib/src/pairing.rs) proves agreeing: the previous version sets the default locale the new one lowers under; a library static shared without --before-classpath; two unrelated RuntimeExceptions, and IllegalArgumentException against a subclass, compared by category; a scope that is false everywhere but sets the default locale before both calls. All five were Verified on the checker at lupovnmv. The order of the calls is observable: with the versions' roles swapped, and with --before-classpath, the shared-static case is a violation.

commits.summary: Countermodels of observed class initializers and of class files the tool read where a JVM reads another: three handed to the evidence stream, two refused
commits.body:
Challenge stream, item 2. lib/tests/fixtures/observed-countermodels holds five fixtures, and lib/tests/observed_countermodels.rs holds each to what a JVM prints. Each was a false proof on the checker as it was (yypzyxmw): crossed, the outside review's A.<clinit> { B.x = 1; k = 7; } (result == 0 proved, a JVM gives 1); lowered, "I".toLowerCase() observed in a Turkish JVM (result == 305 proved, and the locale assumption gone from the result); configured, System.getProperty observed with the property set; released, a class of a multi-release JAR (the tool read the base file where a JVM 17+ loads META-INF/versions/17, so result == 1 was proved where a JVM gives 20, and an observation of the versioned class was put on the base file's code); shadowed, a class path copy of the JDK's org.xml.sax.helpers.AttributesImpl (result == 42 proved, a JVM gives 0).

The first three are the evidence stream's to fix (its brief's item 5 binds an observation): the checker-side test is in the fixtures' README and is sent to its inbox as a failure item. The last two are holes in the class path reader, which no stream owns, so they are refused here: ClassPath::refused (lib/src/classpath.rs) refuses by name, on load and when a class is copied for a pair, a class a multi-release JAR holds a versioned file of, and a class an entry holds in a package of the JDK's image, unless its file is the image's own byte for byte or one of the tool's models (the tool puts both on class paths itself; a first, broader version failed 13 tests for that reason). Enumerating every class still reads the first file, so that walks over which classes exist see it. Not covered: an override only a versioned file declares, and resources.

commits.summary: The challenge stream records its evidence inbox item and a trace error the preservation stream's sync.py put on its line
Countermodels of a checked summary: seven false proofs past the foundation's refusals, refused
commits.body:
Item 3 of the challenge brief. Seven lemmas were proved and their summaries made the checker prove properties a JVM contradicts (fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/lemma-countermodels, its README has the table).

The first group is an initializer cycle that calls the lemma's method before the final static field it reads is written (seen and heldSeen: proved 7, a JVM gives 0). The foundation's guard looked only at the method's own class.

The second is a final static whose initializer, run by the lemma's proof in the harness's state, reads what a caller changes before it initializes the class: a static (setThenOwn), the default locale (turkishThenLowered) and another class's array (setThenCopied).

The third is a StringBuilder a final static holds, read by the model directly or through a method reference (appendThenLogged and appendThenLoggedThroughLambda). The model's reads never asked Engine::reads.

Summaries are no stream's this run, so they are refused here (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs, strings.rs). No summary is used while any class is being initialized; the call runs as written, so seen and heldSeen are now violations, as on a JVM. Class initializers a lemma's proof runs are held to the lemma's read gate, and objects there when one starts or returns count as there before the call. A lemma reads no StringBuilder that was there before the call.

Tried and found guarded, each with its guard named in the README: a lambda's captured array, the ArrayList model, reflection, self-recursive and mutual lemmas, Pattern and Matcher, model statics, and an induction measure.

Audit: the only lemma in use is PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch (286, 288). It has no statics or initializer, calls only String methods, and is never called from an initializer, so 286's decided result is not affected.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a loop invariant, found guarded; three modelled reads of an array a lemma made no refusal of, refused
commits.body: Item 4 of the challenge brief: seven loops whose late iterations do what the first ones do not (a local written once another reaches 5, statics a callee writes, an array under two names, a relation between two cells, an object reached through an array's cell, nested loops, a 100-cell table at a computed index), in lib/tests/fixtures/loop-countermodels with lib/tests/loop_countermodels.rs. At --unwind 2 none is proved (each is no verdict, its witness spurious, the loop named) and at --unwind 7 late is refuted; the README names what in loops.rs guards each. Reading the array models for it found three false proofs of item 3's kind: a lemma about T.clone()[0], Arrays.copyOf(T, 1)[0] and MessageDigest.isEqual(KEY, {0}) over final static arrays was proved and stood in for a caller that writes the array first (a JVM: 5, 5, 0), since Engine::reads was asked of an array load only. Each, and String.join's array, now refuses an array that was there before the call (mod.rs, bytes.rs, regex.rs); fixtures in lemma-countermodels (Cloned) and a new test in lemma_countermodels.rs. Audit: 287's fixed-guard and fixed-security rest on loop invariants and are not affected; the only lemma in use (simpleMatch, 286/288) reads no array. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (the whole Rust default tier, 4 of 4 passed) after estimate and tag.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the fresh pair of versions: a scope that writes the caller's array, and two exception classes of one name, each proved to agree
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge brief, against the preservation stream's zmvkptqz (lib/src/pairing.rs: each version from a fresh state, an exception compared by its class's name). Two pairs of versions a caller tells apart when each runs alone on a JVM are each Verified, non-vacuous, on the preservation line's checker (built apart). first: the scope is called on the caller's own arrays and each version's copy is taken after it, so a scope that zeroes a cell makes the versions agree (alone on {5}: 5 against 0); this line's checker proves it too. failing: two classes named app.Failure, one an IllegalArgumentException and one an IllegalStateException, are one answer by name, though a caller's handler catches one and not the other. Fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/fresh-pair-countermodels with the commands, the audit and the checker-side test, which fails on both there; lib/tests/fresh_pair_countermodels.rs (tool tier) holds them to a JVM. The pairing is the preservation stream's, so no refusal is committed: the test goes to it as a failure item. Audit: 288-290's allowed changes only read; 289's and 290's accepted preservation answers are already refused by the evidence stream's ymzlyksq until a rerun. Verified: test_costs.py run --changed (default tier, 38 binaries) passed; estimate and tag.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the models on request under assumed gaps: three collections a gap makes, each proved empty where a JVM finds one element
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge stream, against the state stream's models on request of ArrayDeque and HashSet (kztoupry). Under --gaps assume, a constructor or method a model does not keep makes an object with no field written. The model's size() then reads those fields, though without the model that call has no assume form. The fixture mc.Gapped (lib/tests/fixtures/model-countermodels) has three cases: ArrayDeque.clone(), whose stated assumptions are all true of the JDK; ArrayDeque(Collection); and ArrayList(Collection), which also reproduces on this line. Each is Verified as result == 0 on the state stream's checker (qrqtplwq), and a JVM gives 1. lib/tests/model_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM. The checker-side test is in the README, where it fails on all three on the state stream's line, and goes to that stream through its inbox, since the models are its this run. The README also lists what was tried and found guarded: the left-out methods under strict, HashSet(int) under advised, a key whose hash changes, a lemma over a deque, and the exception classes. Audit: no example task runs under --gaps assume, so no accepted result is affected. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (it passed) and the checker-side test run on a copy of the state stream's tree.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a write set: a protected field written before a declared exception, and through one bean passed twice, each proved unchanged
commits.body:
Challenge stream, item 5, against the state stream's write set (qrqtplwq, prove --writes). The frame is conjoined to the assertion, so it is read only after a normal return and only on distinct object inputs. lib/tests/fixtures/frame-countermodels/fc/Framed.java has three methods that a JVM sees writing the protected admin field, each Verified on the state checker built apart at qrqtplwq and at vwktulky. Bean#rename, under --throws 'java.lang.IllegalArgumentException when length < 0', sets admin and then throws. Bean#promote(other), with the write set other.admin, does it when called as b.promote(b). Static grant(from, to), with the write set to.admin, does it when called as grant(b, b). lib/tests/frame_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM. The README has the table, the commands, the fix options and the checker-side test, which fails on all three on the state line. That test goes to domain-advances-state as a failure item, since the write set is its rule this run, so no refusal is committed here.

Tried and found guarded: a write through a callee, a lambda or a recursion (refuted by the frame); Locale.setDefault (refused by name); a StringBuilder parameter (not taken); an inherited field (fields_of refuses a subclass). The identity of a String field after 16 String operations matches JDK 25 or is a gap. Audit: no example task passes --writes on any line, so no accepted result rests on these holes. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (passed) and the checker-side test run on both state commits (fails, as it should). Progress also records state-I004, and the evidence session's trace stamps on mqkqvvmw and yypzyxmw for the watcher.

commits.summary: Countermodels of an effect contract at a call: a final static set from a caller's setting, one bean passed twice, and a subclass argument, each a caller's property proved where a JVM breaks it
commits.body:
The state stream's vwktulky lets a setter's checked write set (a lemma with writes:) stand in for its calls through a stub that makes the stated writes. Three callers in lib/tests/fixtures/effect-countermodels each have a proved contract and a property that is Verified on that checker (built apart) while a JVM breaks it. lockedLevel: the setter reads a final static that its class's initializer takes from Config.locked, which the caller sets first, and the contract's proof initialized the class fresh (a JVM gives 0 for 5). pairedLevel: bean.setBoth(bean, mine, theirs) writes the argument's field and then the receiver's, while the stub writes in the writes: order, and the contract's proof never passes one object twice (a JVM gives mine). linkedAdmin: an argument of a subclass whose override, called by the setter, grants admin, since only the receiver's class is checked to be exact.

lib/tests/effect_countermodels.rs holds the fixtures to a JVM. The README has the checker-side test, which fails on all three at vwktulky; it goes to domain-advances-state as a failure item, since the effect contract is that stream's this run, so no refusal is committed here. Also recorded: an exceptional exit does not carry into a caller (throws: is refused, and an undeclared throw refutes the contract, tried), aliasing does, and prove --may-alias this,other already makes the frame refute the earlier promote countermodel. The stub writes a nested object-parameter class with its $, which javac rejects (a refusal). Audit: no example task uses a writes: lemma or --writes on any line. test_costs run --changed and lint pass. The brief is not wrong.
